skill.name: anndata
skill.description: Guidance for using AnnData to create, store, inspect, concatenate, and optimize annotated matrices for single-cell and scverse workflows.
skill.summary: Guides creation, I/O, concatenation, and memory-aware use of AnnData datasets.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: The static command, sensitive-file, blocker, and network hits are false positives caused by Markdown fences, placeholders, documentation links, and AnnData terminology. One low-severity semantic issue remains: the skill steers users toward the author's hosted K-Dense Web service for complex workflows. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, exfiltration, or automatic command execution.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the proactive K-Dense Web recommendation or make it a clearly labeled optional resource chosen by the user.
State that agents should only fetch user-approved datasets from trusted URLs when using remote AnnData examples.

content.value_statement: Single-cell projects often need clean H5AD storage, metadata alignment, and memory-aware loading. This skill guides AnnData structure, file I/O, concatenation, and common scverse workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains AnnData components such as X, obs, var, layers, obsm, obsp, and uns.
Shows how to read and write H5AD, Zarr, CSV, Loom, MTX, and 10X files.
Guides backed mode, sparse matrices, categoricals, and chunked processing for large datasets.
Documents concatenation across batches, modalities, layers, pairwise annotations, and lazy collections.
Covers metadata alignment, raw data storage, common pitfalls, and integration with Scanpy.
limitations: It does not run analysis or validate biological conclusions by itself.
It relies on the user's installed Python packages and local data access.
Remote data examples require user-approved URLs and trusted sources.
It gives AnnData guidance, not a full replacement for Scanpy or scvi-tools workflows.

use_cases.title: Prepare H5AD study files
use_cases.description: Create well-structured AnnData objects with aligned cell metadata, gene metadata, layers, and embeddings.

use_cases.title: Optimize large dataset storage
use_cases.description: Choose backed mode, sparse matrices, categorical metadata, compression, and Zarr chunks for memory-aware access.

use_cases.title: Combine batches safely
use_cases.description: Concatenate experiments while preserving batch labels, merge rules, metadata consistency, and downstream Scanpy compatibility.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic AnnData Object
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new matrix and metadata table.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create an AnnData object from a cell by gene matrix. Explain where cell metadata and gene metadata should go.

prompt_templates.title: Read and Save H5AD Data
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate file I/O with storage choices.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through reading an H5AD file, checking its key components, and saving an optimized copy with compression.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Batch Concatenation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an AnnData concatenation plan for multiple batches. Include join strategy, batch labels, merge behavior, and metadata checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Large Dataset Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my AnnData workflow for a very large dataset. Focus on backed mode, sparse storage, views, copies, and safe metadata alignment.

output_examples.input: I need to merge three H5AD batches before Scanpy analysis.
output: Recommended using observation-axis concatenation with explicit batch labels.
Suggested an inner join for shared genes unless missing genes must be retained.
Added checks for duplicated observation names, inconsistent gene identifiers, and layer compatibility.

output_examples.input: My AnnData file is too large to load into memory.
output_examples.output: The response recommends backed mode for inspection, sparse matrices for count data, categorical metadata, and chunked processing before loading subsets.

output_examples.input: I am confused about obs, var, obsm, layers, and uns.
output_examples.output: The response maps each AnnData slot to its role, gives examples of typical contents, and explains how dimensions should align.

best_practices: Use backed mode or Zarr when data is larger than available memory.
Align external metadata by observation or variable index before assignment.
Store raw data before filtering when downstream comparisons need original values.
anti_patterns: Do not repeatedly subset large AnnData objects inside tight loops without a performance plan.
Do not assign metadata by row order when indexes can be matched directly.
Do not use dense matrices for sparse count data unless memory cost is acceptable.

faq.question: What is AnnData used for?
faq.answer: AnnData stores annotated matrices with observations, variables, metadata, embeddings, layers, and unstructured analysis results.

faq.question: Does this skill replace Scanpy?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on the AnnData data structure. Scanpy provides broader analysis workflows built on AnnData.

faq.question: Can it help with very large H5AD files?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains backed mode, sparse storage, categoricals, Zarr, chunking, and memory-aware access patterns.

faq.question: Can it combine multiple datasets?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers AnnData concatenation, join choices, merge strategies, batch labels, and metadata consistency checks.

faq.question: Does it download data automatically?
faq.answer: No. Remote access examples require a user-approved URL and trusted source before any data is fetched.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
